closedGreenOrHonestPartial: HONEST PARTIAL, leaning strongly resolved. This lane found and reproduced, with live evidence, a genuine code defect in the rail's own city-to-layer resolution that explains the refusal far more precisely than any of the dispatch's three named mechanisms. It also found that even after that defect is corrected, the rail's own (correctly-scoped) measured residue is genuinely above the declared ceiling for both counties -- a real, modest gap, not fabricated by the defect. It is a partial close because fixing the defect and re-deriving the ceiling are both real work this dispatch's dry-run-only mandate does not authorize, and because time did not extend to a full live-ArcGIS audit of whether the multi-layer defect class (as opposed to the S-P missing-code class) exists anywhere else in the six-county program beyond confirming Elgin is the only CURRENT multi-layer city in the staged table.
missionPremise: P-124 CTX-REFUSAL dispatch (_dispatches/2026-09-09_ctx-refusal_dispatch.md), successor to CTX-ELGIN. CTX-ELGIN established the 9/457 ceiling as correct per its own probe and could not read hauska-factory (out of its scope) to see what the rail itself actually measures; it flagged 'a hauska-factory-side consumer calling tx_zoning_district_staging directly' as the one thing it could not rule out. This lane's job was to read that rail's own query, run its own dry run, and resolve why factory-parcel-r5-zoning refuses LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED against a ceiling CTX-ELGIN confirmed correct.

Not satisfied: the code fix itself, and a fresh, individually control-validated re-probe of the corrected 36/507 residues, both correctly out of this dispatch's dry-run-only mandate and named as recommendations instead.

theRailsResidueDefinition.guard: assertResidueWithinDeclaration, called from processCity in src/jobs/parcel-r5-zoning.mjs, throwing LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED
theRailsResidueDefinition.population: ALL in-city parcels for the city's place_fips, per CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL (landing_parcel_jurisdiction, disposition='in-city', county_fips in the six-county PROGRAM_FIPS list) -- computed fresh every run, NOT filtered or gated by any current parcel_record_cell state. This is the SAME population definition as CTX-STAGE2/CTX-ELGIN's staged-table join (instrument B), NOT the dispatch's hypothesized 'rail's own already-narrowed unaccounted-cell set' (that population belongs to a DIFFERENT instrument, scripts/ctx-w2/city-residue-coverage.mjs, which is not what this guard reads).
theRailsResidueDefinition.predicate: A live spatial join, this run, of txgio_parcel parcel geometry (ring, or a bbox-centre fallback when ring geometry is unusable) against zone polygons decoded fresh from tx_zoning_district_staging (city_key = the specific row being processed, layer_role='base'), via ST_Covers for a full ring-in-zone match or ST_Intersects with a 1e-8 deg2 area floor otherwise, best match by overlap area. This is CLOSER to instrument B (both read tx_zoning_district_staging) than instrument A (which never touches this table), but is NOT instrument B's exact predicate: instrument B used ST_Contains(ST_PointOnSurface(parcel), zone) -- a point test; the rail uses true polygon overlap with an area floor, a materially different and generally more permissive test.
theRailsResidueDefinition.exclusions: None at the population level (every in-city parcel of the county is in scope). At the zone-polygon level: only rows in tx_zoning_district_staging for that exact city_key and layer_role='base' with non-null, valid, non-empty decoded geometry (verified live: zero rows dropped by the decode step for elgin-tx -- 3,209 raw, 3,209 decoded).

instrumentB_stagedTableJoin_ctxStage2And.predicate: ST_Contains(ST_PointOnSurface(parcel), zoning polygon) against tx_zoning_district_staging, run as an ad hoc measurement mirroring hauska-engine's join-zoning-district-to-parcels.mjs.

instrumentD_theRail_thisLane.result_when_correctly_scoped_per_county_: 36 (48021, against the 3,209-polygon elgin-tx/Bastrop-side layer) / 507 (48453, against the 499-polygon elgin-tx-travis/Travis-side layer).
instrumentD_theRail_thisLane.result_as_actually_produced_in_an_unfilt: Whichever of Elgin's two city_key rows processes first determines what number the guard actually throws with for Bastrop -- either the real 36, or a spurious cross-layer 3,288 -- because of the ordering hazard described below. Travis's number is symmetrically corrupted the same way if the other row processes first.

theThreeDefinitions_sideBySide.apples_to_apples_verdict: NOT apples to apples with any of the three, and the mismatch is worse than a simple population/predicate disagreement. The declared ceiling (9/457) was derived from instrument A. The guard that enforces it reads instrument D (this lane's designation), whose CORRECT population matches instrument B's (not A's) and whose predicate matches neither A nor B exactly. Worse: instrument D's population scoping has its own defect (below) that, in unfiltered production, can additionally corrupt the number it compares to the ceiling into something with no relationship to the real GIS gap at all. Three genuine disagreements are stacked: (1) ceiling vs. guard population, (2) ceiling vs. guard predicate, (3) guard's own internal correctness bug when a city spans multiple staged layers.

mechanismResolved.chosen: A confirmed code defect in the rail's own city-to-layer resolution -- closest to the dispatch's Mechanism C ('the rail's own query has a defect'), but far more specific than 'unread and unknown': loadInScopeCities (IN_SCOPE_CITIES_SQL) returns one row per (place_fips, city_key), and Elgin has two live, correctly-staged base layers under two different city_keys (elgin-tx = FeatureServer/0, Bastrop-side, 3,209 polygons; elgin-tx-travis = FeatureServer/1, Travis-side, 499 polygons, staged by CTX-STAGE2). processCity's population query (CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL) scopes by place_fips alone -- the WHOLE city, both counties -- never intersecting with the county that particular city_key row's own layer actually covers. Verified live: matching all 5,455 Elgin parcels against ONLY the Bastrop-side layer gives Bastrop residue 36 (real) and Travis residue 1,680 (spurious -- Travis parcels tested against a layer that structurally cannot cover them); matching against ONLY the Travis-side layer gives Travis residue 507 (real, close to instruments A and B) and Bastrop residue 3,288 (equally spurious in the other direction). A second, independent defect compounds this: IN_SCOPE_CITIES_SQL's own ORDER BY (in_city_parcels DESC, no tiebreaker) does not deterministically order Elgin's two tied rows, so an unfiltered production sweep can surface either the real Bastrop number (36) or the spurious cross-layer one (3,288) for the identical refusal code on identical underlying data, purely by chance of sort order.
mechanismResolved.secondMechanismConsidered: The dispatch's own Mechanism A -- the rail counts a narrower, already-earned-state-excluded 'unaccounted cells' population, so the probe (9) and the rail could both be correct about different questions.
mechanismResolved.whyRejected: Directly falsified by reading assertResidueWithinDeclaration's call site. layerGapByCounty, the Map the guard actually checks, is built by iterating every row CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL returns -- the full, un-gated in-city population -- with no join or filter against parcel_record_cell's current cell_state at all. The population Mechanism A describes (already-narrowed unaccounted cells) IS real and IS measured in this codebase, but by a different instrument entirely (scripts/ctx-w2/city-residue-coverage.mjs, whose header explicitly frames itself as 'the population the GATE actually scores' -- which turns out to describe a DIFFERENT gate, requireCountyPopulation in publish-readiness-gate.mjs, not LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED). Confirmed empirically too: the rail's live Bastrop residue (36) does not match either the narrowed unaccounted-cell figure CTX-ELGIN quoted for the same county at gate time (26) or the value that would result from filtering to only currently-unaccounted rows; it matches exactly what a full-population, unfiltered spatial join against the correct layer produces.
mechanismResolved.residualGapNotExplainedByEitherDefect: Even after correctly scoping each county to its own layer, the rail's real, defect-free measurement (36 Bastrop, 507 Travis) is still above the declared ceiling (9, 457) by a modest, comparable margin (27 and 50 parcels respectively) in both counties. This is NOT explained by either defect above -- it is a genuine, if modest, disagreement between instrument A's point-in-polygon predicate and the rail's polygon-overlap predicate, run today against the current (CTX-ELGIN-restaged) layer state. Not investigated further here (would require the same per-parcel geometric control-validation CTX-ELGIN did for its own 9/457, which is new probing work, not something a dry run of the existing rail can settle).

spDecompositionAndOtherCities.sPClassRecap: CTX-ELGIN found 11 live Elgin_Zoning (Bastrop-side) polygons carrying Zone_Code='S-P', absent from hauska-engine's codeDomainMap allow-list, so those polygons never get staged at all -- 9 of the 11 geometrically cover 10 of the residue parcels. This class (a live code silently excluded before staging, in a per-city allow-list that lives in hauska-engine's registry.ts) is NOT visible to hauska-factory: the rail only ever sees what already made it into tx_zoning_district_staging. Confirmed live from this repo: elgin-tx's 3,209 staged rows decode 1:1 into r5_zones_ok with zero drops, meaning whatever codeDomainMap excluded upstream is invisible here by construction, not something hauska-factory's own query could detect or be checked against for another city without reading hauska-engine's registry.ts (out of this dispatch's repo scope, same boundary CTX-ELGIN itself respected for legacy-design-tools). This class's cross-city prevalence is therefore an open question this lane cannot answer and does not attempt to guess at.
spDecompositionAndOtherCities.newClassFoundThisLane: A structurally different defect class, fully visible and fully checkable from within hauska-factory: a city split across county lines with more than one separately-staged base zoning layer under distinct city_keys. Checked directly: SELECT city_geo_id, array_agg(DISTINCT city_key) FROM tx_zoning_district_staging WHERE layer_role='base' GROUP BY city_geo_id HAVING count(DISTINCT city_key) > 1. Result: exactly one city_geo_id (4823044 / Elgin) currently qualifies. No other city in the six-county program is currently split across multiple staged base layers.
spDecompositionAndOtherCities.caveat: This bounds CURRENT exposure only, measured against today's staged data. The underlying code defect (population scoped by place_fips without intersecting the layer's actual county coverage) is latent in loadInScopeCities/processCity for ANY future multi-county, multi-layer city, independent of whether one exists today.

proposedFixes_notApplied: Fix 1 (the layer/population scoping defect): when a place_fips resolves to more than one city_key row (a multi-layer city), either (a) intersect each city_key row's parcel population with the specific county_fips its own staged layer's geometry/bbox actually falls in rather than using the whole place_fips indiscriminately, or (b) collapse a multi-layer city to ONE processCity pass per place_fips against the UNION of all its layers' zone polygons -- recommended, since buildZoningCells already records sourceUrl per matched parcel from whichever zone row matched it, so per-layer provenance survives a union without needing separate passes. Either fix also removes the ORDER BY tie hazard, since there would be exactly one pass (not two racing for which throws first) per multi-layer city.

Fix 2 (the ceiling): DECLARED_LAYER_GAP.Elgin.expectedResidue (9/457) was derived from instrument A, not from the rail's own predicate. Recommend re-probing with the rail's own corrected, per-county-correct-layer method (36 Bastrop / 507 Travis, once Fix 1 lands) and individually control-validating the delta parcels (27 Bastrop, 50 Travis) the same way CTX-ELGIN validated its original 9/457, before revising the declared ceiling -- per the declaration's own stated design principle, an exact ceiling must be 'actually probed,' not widened to match whatever the code currently returns.

leave_behind.text: As of 2026-09-09 (live, this session): tx_zoning_district_staging holds city_key='elgin-tx' (3,209 rows, Bastrop-side FeatureServer/0, CTX-ELGIN's restage) and city_key='elgin-tx-travis' (499 rows, Travis-side FeatureServer/1, CTX-STAGE2's stage), both city_geo_id='4823044', both layer_role='base'. loadInScopeCities returns BOTH as separate rows for place_fips=23044, each carrying the full 5,455-parcel in-city population.

Live dry run, 2026-09-09: runParcelR5Zoning(apply=false, --city elgin-tx) throws LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED with actualResidue=36, declaredCeiling=9 for 48021. Reproduced twice, byte-identical. Travis's own residue against its correct layer (elgin-tx-travis, 499 polygons) measured separately at 507 against a declared ceiling of 457, also over.

A city that spans two counties with two independently-staged ArcGIS layers under two different city_keys is not one row to this rail's own city-resolution query -- it is two, and each row's parcel population is scoped by the whole city (place_fips) rather than by the county its own layer covers. Any per-city spatial-join rail whose population query is 'this whole city' but whose zone-polygon pool is 'this one layer' will silently manufacture residue for whichever county doesn't belong to that layer, and the size of the false residue can be enormous (1,680 of 1,706, or 3,288 of 3,749) -- large enough to look like a real, dramatic GIS gap rather than a wrong-layer artifact, unless someone runs the layers in isolation and cross-checks county-by-county, as this lane did.

Two SQL instruments in this same repo (assertResidueWithinDeclaration's live layerGapByCounty, and scripts/ctx-w2/city-residue-coverage.mjs's parcel_record_cell census) both describe themselves, in comments or by role, as measuring 'the residue' or 'the population the gate actually scores' for the same rail -- and they measure two different things (a fresh full-population spatial join vs. current cell state in a different store). A future reader trusting either comment in isolation would misdescribe what the OTHER one measures. Cross-check an instrument's self-description against its actual SQL before citing it as ground truth for a different gate.

Whether an unfiltered production sweep (no --city filter) actually hit the real Bastrop number (36) or the spurious cross-layer number (3,288) in execution dppvg (the refusal named by the dispatch) is unknown from this lane -- the dispatch does not quote dppvg's exact error message, and this lane deliberately never ran an unfiltered sweep (choosing --city elgin-tx specifically to avoid the ordering hazard while still reproducing the same refusal code). Recommend the integration seat check execution dppvg's actual logged actualResidue value if it is retained anywhere (run_events, Cloud Run logs), since a 3,288 in that log would itself have been strong, immediate evidence of this defect.

Fix 1 (layer/population scoping) and Fix 2 (re-derive the ceiling from the rail's own corrected method) are both real, scoped, evidence-backed follow-on work this lane identified but did not apply, per this dispatch's dry-run-only mandate and its explicit prohibition on changing the ceiling. Recommend a short, separately-dispatched lane for each -- Fix 1 is a hauska-factory code change (in scope for a future hauska-factory lane); Fix 2 requires new live-probe work analogous to CTX-ELGIN's, not just a config edit.

The S-P missing-code class (hauska-engine's codeDomainMap allow-list silently excluding a real, live district code before staging) remains unchecked for cities other than Elgin, because that check requires reading hauska-engine's registry.ts, out of this dispatch's repo scope. The structurally different multi-layer-per-city class this lane found and checked IS fully answered from hauska-factory alone: Elgin is the only current instance.
